result.title: FuGIBench: Evaluating Reliable Preparation in Streaming Video
result.summary: An assistant watching a worker can prepare for an emerging need before the worker is ready to receive help.As the need evolves, the assistant must maintain preparation until a response is due, or withdraw it if the need disappears. Video anticipation and interactive response benchmarks leave this interval between early evidence and response largely unmeasured. We introduce FuGIBench (Future-Grounded Interaction), a streaming-video benchmark in which a model chooses among waiting, reversible preparation, and response given a causal video prefix and a task contract. The benchmark contains 19,893 synthetic tool-assistance videos across ten tool tasks, in handover, ordinary-activity, and cancelled-need tracks. One primary score credits sustained preparation, incorporates response-interval alignment, and penalizes activity when the reference prescribes waiting. On a frozen set of 1,000 episodes, a reference system with a longer preparation lead has poorer response alignment, while similar handover leads accompany different levels of activity during ordinary work in matched scenarios. Together with cancellation analyses, these results show why evaluating preparation requires tracking decisions as needs develop, become actionable, or disappear.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 FuGIBench 流式视频基准，含约两万段合成工具辅助视频，要求模型依据视频前缀在「等待、可逆准备、响应」之间选择，并用兼顾持续准备与响应区间对齐的评分衡量决策时机。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「等待—准备—响应—取消需求」决策轨迹与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 中的停止、撤销和提前行动代价直接相关，可供核查停止准则与动态计算收益的评测设计，但属视频助手场景，与 latent 状态机制的关联需进一步判断。
